evals.prompt: Add unit tests for the useThing hook in packages/foo. Heads up: packages/foo's test:unit runs `vitest run --config ./vitest.config.mts`.
evals.expected_output: Agent detects the package is on Vitest (test:unit runs vitest) and writes vi.* — vi.mock with an async factory + awaited vi.importActual for boundaries, renderHook from @baseapp-frontend/test — NOT jest.* or ts-jest patterns.
assertions: Agent detects the runner is Vitest from the package's test:unit script (does not assume Jest)
Agent uses vi.mock with `async () => ({ ...(await vi.importActual('m')), thing: vi.fn() })` for boundaries
Agent uses renderHook from @baseapp-frontend/test, not @testing-library/react
Agent does NOT emit jest.mock / jest.requireActual for this package
Agent runs the suite via pnpm --filter packages/foo exec vitest run (coverage provider v8)

evals.prompt: Port authentication's useLogout.test.tsx to the Vitest comparison lane (*.vitest.test.tsx). The original mocks @tanstack/react-query and @baseapp-frontend/utils and uses a `const mockResetQueries = jest.fn()` referenced inside the mock factory.
evals.expected_output: Agent applies the Vitest porting rules: outer-var mock fns move to vi.hoisted (vi.mock can't reference outer vars), factories become async with awaited vi.importActual, default-export modules get a `default`.
assertions: Agent moves `mockResetQueries` into `const { mockResetQueries } = vi.hoisted(() => ({ mockResetQueries: vi.fn() }))`
Agent converts jest.mock factories to async with `...(await vi.importActual(...))`
Agent explains vi.mock is hoisted above the file and cannot reference outer variables (no jest mock-prefix escape hatch)
Agent does not leave `jest.requireActual` or a non-async importActual factory

evals.prompt: My Vitest test throws 'Cannot access mockFetch before initialization'. I have `const mockFetch = vi.fn()` at the top and reference it inside `vi.mock('@baseapp-frontend/utils', () => ({ baseAppFetch: mockFetch }))`.
evals.expected_output: Agent diagnoses the vi.mock hoisting rule and fixes it with vi.hoisted (or by inlining vi.fn() in the factory), explaining why Jest's mock-prefix trick doesn't apply in Vitest.
assertions: Agent identifies that vi.mock is hoisted above the const, so the outer variable isn't initialized yet
Agent fixes it via `const { mockFetch } = vi.hoisted(() => ({ mockFetch: vi.fn() }))`
Agent notes this differs from Jest (no `mock`-prefixed outer-var exception in Vitest)

Agent sets up vitest.config.mts (jsdom, @vitejs/plugin-react, v8 coverage) and test:unit running vitest run
Agent uses the @baseapp-frontend/test wrapper + boundary-only mocking conventions
Agent does not default the new package to Jest
